chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Abū Baṣīr, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, he said:

I asked him about a man performing tamattuʿ who did not find what he could offer as hady, until when it was the Day of Nafr he found the price of a sheep. Should he slaughter, or should he fast? He said: Rather, he should fast, for the days of slaughter have already passed.

So this does not contradict what we have stated, because what is meant in this report is one who did not find the hady nor its price and fasted three days, then later found the price of the hady. It is upon him to fast whatever remains due upon him to complete the ten days, and the hady is not obligatory upon him. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ الذَّبْحِ: the appointed days in which slaughtering the hady is valid
key_terms.الْعَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: the full ten days of fasting required as substitution
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial offering required in this pilgrimage context
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the initial three days of fasting in place of hady
key_terms.ثَمَنَ شَاةٍ: the price of a sheep for sacrificial offering
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّفْرِ: the day of departure from Mina after the rites

ai.seo_question: If a pilgrim in tamattuʿ finds the price of a sheep only after the days of sacrifice, should he offer hady or fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the pilgrim performing tamattuʿ who cannot obtain the hady during the appointed days. If he only finds the price of a sheep on the Day of Nafr, he does not slaughter but instead completes the prescribed fasting, because the days of sacrifice have already passed.
